name: Holy Grail Skin Co.
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. Atlanta Magazine (Nov 2025) calls Holy Grail Skin Co. a "Newcomer" that launched in April 2025, founded by two Atlanta moms (Mary Peck and Leah Matthews) after roughly two years of R&D. That is well within the ~2-year launch window. The company sells DTC through its own Shopify-style site, with a single product (Elixir no. 1) and a refill subscription. There is no evidence of national retail distribution. The website and magazine mention no outside funding or parent company. The Tracxn results about 'Holy Grail' (Y Combinator, Accel, seed rounds from 2019/2021) and GRAIL (cancer diagnostics) refer to different, unrelated companies, and the e-l.f. 'holy grail' result is only a generic phrase. None of these relate to this skincare brand. The 'Best of Atlanta' award and press coverage show local traction but not scale or funding. The company is a recent, small, DTC, apparently unfunded and independent startup.
founders_supported_explanation: Both people are shown as co-founders of Holy Grail Skin Co. The company site says 'Leah + Mary, Co-Founders, Holy Grail Skin Co.', and the About page is signed 'Mary + Leah' and says 'Before we were founders'. The About page also says Mary serves on the Bettie Brand Fund's Board of Directors, and the podcast listing calls 'Mary and Leah' the founders of Holy Grail Skin Care. The failed claims: (1) Leah Matthews. Her LinkedIn profile lists her as Co-Founder at Holy Grail Skin Co. since Apr 2025, and the Studio Go and Studio To Go details match it. But the company site names the co-founder only as 'Leah', and no source ties that Leah to the LinkedIn profile. The agent says this itself, so the Leah Matthews identity link and her LinkedIn background are not confirmed as the same person. (2) Mary. The co-founder role and the Board of Directors detail are backed by the company site. The agent also flags the podcast name mismatch, which is a minor spelling difference ('Skin Care' vs 'Skin Co.'). The role field says 'Co-Founders' (plural), which is a small wording issue. No last name is given in any source. Overall, the names and founder roles are right, but the full name and background for Leah Matthews are not confirmed as hers.

name: Stellar Beauty Co.
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the agent's claim. Business Wire says Stellar Beauty Co. launched July 9, 2026, exclusively DTC at stellarbeautyco.com, so it is brand new. Beauty Independent reports the parents self-funded it, and no VC round appears anywhere in the evidence. The footprint is small: four SKUs, about 5,000 TikTok followers, and no retail distribution. It is a family-run startup with no sign of ownership by a larger company. The Yahoo Finance result about Madison Reed and the Tracxn list of other beauty brands are unrelated companies. One minor discrepancy is that Beauty Independent lists prices of $12-$27 while the agent said $16-$27, but this does not affect the stage conclusion.
founders_supported_explanation: Every part of the claim is backed by the cited pages. Business Wire and Yahoo Finance call Stella Dorazio the 'founder' of Stellar Beauty Co. and describe her as a 12-year-old athlete. They also say the brand was inspired by her experience balancing sports, school, camps and everyday adventures. YPulse says a class project at age 9 led her to launch the brand, and Beauty Independent says the same. Beauty Independent also says Stella and her mother Mallory worked together on product research, formulation and packaging. Trendhunter additionally confirms her as founder. No claim failed.

name: Burd Beauty
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the agent's claim. The brand launched on Oct 22, 2025, so it is only months old. It sells only through its own Shopify site, TikTok Shop and Instagram, and national retail is only planned. It has just two products, a shampoo and a conditioner, plus a set. No funding round appears anywhere in the evidence. The only funding article from the independent search is about Madison Reed, an unrelated company. Co-founder Julie Smolyansky is CEO of publicly traded Lifeway Foods, but the sources describe her as a co-founder acting personally. Nothing says Lifeway owns or operates Burd, and the site lists a personal Gmail contact. So it looks like an independent family-founded startup.
founders_supported_explanation: All three claims are backed by the cited pages. Leah Burdeen: the press release, About page, Preferred Health and Instagram bio all name her as a founder or co-founder. The press release gives age 17, the Associate Producer role on several documentaries including an Oscar-contending film, and the student-led analog photography organization. The 'Lead Burdeen' quote is in the release and is described accurately as a likely typo. The Instagram bio lists @leah_burdeen. Misha Burdeen: she is quoted as co-founder, and the release gives age 15, sophomore, patent-pending package designer whose designs inspired Burd's aesthetic, cheerleader, and advocate for mental health and self-expression. Julie Smolyansky: the release quotes her as 'CEO of Lifeway Foods and co-founder of Burd Beauty'. It says she became the youngest female CEO of a publicly traded company at age 27, co-wrote Chicago's first teen dating violence prevention curriculum in 1991, produced The Hunting Ground, and co-founded Test400K. No claim failed.

name: VIBES Beverages
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early stage on every criterion. Launch: the official launch was May 15, 2026, with three SKUs, and the product pages and blog content date from 2026. Funding: no priced VC round appears anywhere. The Tracxn results (Series A/B, Accel, Fidelity) are for a different company named "Vibes" (an unrelated mobile marketing firm) and don't apply to this beverage LLC. Footprint: sales are mainly DTC via Shopify plus kava bars and specialty/on-premise accounts, and the wholesale page and press releases describe retail partnerships as only "entering key markets" or "actively expanding", with no named national chain. Independence: it is an independent LLC co-manufactured by Burma Brewing, a contract manufacturer, and is run by five co-founders, not a subsidiary of a larger company. The "nationwide" launch language is marketing for DTC shipping and not national retail presence.
founders_supported_explanation: All five founder claims are backed by the cited pages. The BevNET and Brewbound press release names five co-founders. It gives Strain as Co-Founder and Chief Brand Officer, who co-founded Super Top Secret in 2009 and brings two decades of experience. It gives Gupta as Co-Founder and Head of Marketing, and Co-Founder of Total Botanical Solutions. It gives Willardsen as Co-Founder and Head of Activation and Growth, with the Nitro Circus/Thrillbillies and Stunt Run 5K background. Croxford is called Co-Founder in his quote and the media-contact line. The release also describes his 15+ years of experience in the 'Growth Strategist' section, where he is named by surname only, and the claim itself says so. The August release also calls him co-founder. Abate is called Co-Founder and a founder of Mitra9, and the release lists his Vibes responsibilities. His LinkedIn confirms Co-Founder at Vibes, Co-Founder at Mitra9 Brands (Dec 2020 to Jul 2024), and Chief Commercial Officer at Burma Brewing (Jan 2025 to present). The Vibes company LinkedIn page lists him as Co-Founder. No claims failed.

name: Happy Panda
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early stage. Happy Panda's official market launch was announced via PR Newswire on Feb 2, 2026, so it launched very recently. It sells DTC from drinkhappypanda.com, and its LinkedIn page says it is seeking retail relationships in Florida and distributor relationships, so it has no national retail footprint. LinkedIn lists it as 'Self-Owned' with only 34 followers, so it is not part of a larger company. The independent search turned up no funding for it: the Panda Retail, Cheeky Panda, Asset Panda and Panda Express results are different companies. The founders are two individuals with no sign of a priced VC round. Nationwide shipping is DTC, not retail. The unverified funding status leaves some uncertainty, but nothing contradicts the early-stage label.
founders_supported_explanation: Every claim checks out against the cited pages. Cameron James: the about-us page lists him as 'Founder & CEO' and describes him as an 'IFBB pro turned sales mogul and lifestyle entrepreneur.' The Mar 2026 PR Newswire release says Happy Panda was founded by Dr. Noor A. and Cameron James and quotes him as 'co-founder and CEO.' The Sept 2026 release calls him 'Co-Founder Cameron James.' The Feb 2026 release gives his background (deep roots in professional sports and fitness, accolades in music and high-level sales, met Dr. Noor in the health insurance sector) and refers to him as 'Cam.' The 'Cam' link to Cameron James holds up: the about-us page says 'Cam' for Cameron James, and the Sept 2026 release says the Feb 2026 launch was announced by 'co-founders James and Dr. Noor A.' The 'Cameron Jones' caption in the Mar release is an evident typo, since the same release's text says Cameron James. Dr. Noor A.: the about-us page lists her as 'Founder & COO' and a 'Surgeon turned serial entrepreneur.' The Mar 2026 release quotes her as 'co-founder and COO.' The Feb 2026 release gives her Master's in Public Health and triple specialty training in Internal Medicine, General Surgery, and OB/GYN. It also labels a photo 'Founder Dr. Noor A.', which ties 'Dr. Noor' to 'Dr. Noor A.' No claim failed.

name: Sēkwl Beverage House
early_stage_explanation: Sēkwl launched DTC on May 1, 2025, which is well within the last 2 years. No funding round appears anywhere in the evidence. The only funding page found (Tracxn) is for a different company called "Beverage House" with investors like Accel and Partech, so it doesn't apply. The company is founder-led, with a small team of four co-founders, and has no parent company. Its footprint is small and regional: DTC plus a first regional distribution deal with a Colorado distributor (SMNR Sales) covering Colorado's Front Range and mountains. LinkedIn claims 50+ retail locations "in Colorado and across the U.S.", which is modest and not national retail chain presence. The May 2025 press release mentioned plans for nationwide retail later in the year, but there is no evidence this has happened at scale. The agent's "pre-seed" label is plausible, though funding is unknown. Overall the company is recently launched, bootstrapped as far as the evidence shows, independent, and small, so early-stage holds.
founders_supported_explanation: All four founder claims are backed by the cited pages. Matthew Eaton: the press release and BevNET quote him as 'Founder & Chief Beverage Officer', and the press release says the company was 'Founded by... Matthew Eaton'. The AEDA page describes the idea as born of a personal health scare and his research into turkey tail mushrooms. His LinkedIn lists Head of Responsible Sourcing at Autodesk (Aug 2024 to present) and Senior Manager Strategic Sourcing and Head of Responsible Sourcing at VMware (Jan 2021 to Feb 2024). Ryan Kelley: AEDA names him as a cofounder, and the press release calls him Eaton's husband. The Instagram post only says 'Ryan' is 'co-founder and Head of Operations', but the claim itself flags that this link is by first name only. That is a reasonable inference and not needed for the cofounder status, which AEDA already establishes. Shannon Eurich: AEDA names her as a cofounder, and the press release calls her one of Eaton's best friends. Nothing in the sources states prior experience, which matches the claim. John Walls: AEDA names him as a cofounder. The press release gives his title as 'Chief Storyteller and Head of Marketing & Communications' and lists him as media contact. No prior experience is stated, as the claim says. No claim failed.
